name: Abathur
overview: Abathur plays differently from every other Hero in the game. With extremely low health and negligible Basic Attack damage, he needs to avoid direct confrontations with enemy Heroes. He instead applies pressure to the map through use of his global Abilities, and participates in team fights by empowering his allies with Symbiote. Abathur is very dependent on good strategy, and can greatly benefit from (or suffer on) certain maps and team compositions.
strengths: Can soak multiple lanes at once, creating an XP lead
One of the best split-pushing Heroes in the game
Can teleport anywhere on the map (provided there is vision) using Deep Tunnel
Toxic Nest is excellent at spotting and dismounting enemies attempting to gank allies or sneak objectives
weaknesses: Cannot solo a lane by himself
Body is extremely vulnerable if found
Requires very good multitasking and map awareness
Team must adapt to Abathur's unique gameplay style in order to succeed
Viability is very dependent on the map and team compositions

synergies.explanation: Abathur is strong with Heroes who serve as ideal Symbiote hosts, or who are good targets for Ultimate Evolution. Ideal Symbiote hosts are Heroes that naturally position themselves in melee range, or with mobile assassins, that can easily abuse Symbiote to kill squishy targets.

counters.explanation: Abathur's Symbiote and Locusts help him to deny the enemy team experience when objectives spawn, when most Heroes will need to vacate lanes in order to rotate. This tactic is directly countered by Heroes who can travel globally, and who waveclear very efficiently. He is also very weak against compositions that can join as four to push down a lane. Heroes like Sylvanas, Zarya or Sgt. Hammer are great for that purpose, and for this reason are a big threat for Abathur's team.

maps.explanation: Abathur's win condition is to be more places at once than his enemy, and overwhelm the other team with a constant stream of subtle pressure. Abathur is very strong on large maps that feature frequent objective spawns, which allow him to be somewhat ignored for some of the match. These maps allow him to either soak an advantage, or force the enemy team to split. His strength, however, is also his weakness. Abathur gets very little value on small maps that feature fewer lanes, team fights near lanes, or objectives that do not require immediate rotations. Abathur is excellent on Sky Temple due to Calldown: MULE denying most of objective's shots.

builds.name: Symbiote Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
The Symbiote Build maximises Abathur's team fight presence by taking Talents that improve Symbiote's damage dealing Abilities. This team fight presence comes at the cost of global pressure, as you will lack the huge lane pressure provided by other builds. Although this is not a build that focuses on pushing lanes, it is still important to soak as much experience as possible. Due to the short range of Symbiote's Abilities, this build is ideally paired with a melee assassin who benefits from increased attack speed.

Adrenal Overload will greatly increase the performance of certain heroes, like Illidan, or Greymane. When the Symbiote host is not reliant on Basic Attacks, you should get Needlespine instead. Even though Calldown: MULE will be useful in most games, Vile Nest is also an option in Dragon Shire and Cursed Hollow, since it will provide much control for enemy rotation and objectives. At Level 16 Adrenaline Boost is the standard Talent, but Envenomed Spikes is a great option against team compositions with limited mobility, since the slow will affect all enemies, greatly disrupting their movement. Together with a Dragonblade Genji or Maiev, you can go for Evolutionary Link at Level 20, since the shield and the extra duration will be incredibly good for those Heroes.

builds.name: Toxic Nest Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Toxic Nest build can be a good choice in situations where you do not have viable heroes to place Symbiote on. It excels in maps with constant rotation, such as Dragon Shire, Blackheart's Bay, Cursed Hollow, Garden of Terror and Towers of Doom.

Even though it sounds interesting to use all your Toxic Nest in the same point, this is not the best way to abuse this build. We recommend using the Nests between the waves, while making sure they are not very close between them. The main focus is to abuse Vile Nest's slow to delay enemy rotations or to control the way towards the objective. It is also very important to always have a Toxic Nest on enemy's Mercenary camps, since it will give that information to your team, and sometimes it will even stop their intention in capturing it.

Envenomed Nest is especially strong when your team has a good ganker or roamer, as Toxic Nests can catch enemies during rotations. Together with Vile Nest, affected Heroes are Slowed and have their Armor reduced by 15, giving your ally time to secure the kill. At level 13, Soma Transference is the default pick as long as most of your simbiote hosts are frontline Heroes. Therefore, it is better to go for Spatial Efficiency when backliners are the hosts. Evolutionary Link can be a good Talent as well, and you should use the Heroic Ability on your teammate that is having more trouble staying alive, since the 35% shield will be applied to them, giving them some much needed protection.

builds.name: Locust Strain Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
The Locust Strain Build is strong on large Maps, where Deep Tunnel and Locust Brood allow Abathur to create split-push pressure far from the enemy team. Locusts can sustain themselves through undefended Minion waves, making their pressure harder to answer after Bombard Strain at Level 13 and Survival Instincts at Level 16. When enemies are visible elsewhere, tunnel to an advanced position, use Locust Brood, and retreat. Ultimate Evolution can then be used to assist your team while enemies respond to the Locusts.

At Level 4, Adrenal Overload is excellent when your team has a decent Basic Attacker, such as Illidan or Greymane, who can take full advantage of its bonus Attack Speed. Without such an ally, Prolific Dispersal provides more map control and information through additional Toxic Nests, while Slapathur makes Abathur much harder to dive when facing Heroes such as Genji or Zeratul. At Level 7, Networked Carapace greatly strengthens the push of allied Minion waves, but Calldown: MULE is essential on Sky Temple and Haunted Mines, where repairing Structures helps counter objective pressure.

name: Alarak
overview: Alarak is a melee Assassin who controls the battlefield by manipulating the positioning of his enemies. He can sacrifice raw damage for increased utility through Sadism, allowing him to deal with each challenge differently. Telekinesis allows him to push himself and enemies in any direction, while Discord Strike can render them completely helpless afterward. It is recommended to play him alongside tanks and assassins. He excels at displacing enemies into dangerous positions, enabling easy follow-ups from teammates, securing takedowns. Reliably landing Discord Strike and Telekinesis can be difficult, and requires practice. Putting in the time to get comfortable with these Abilities is essential in leveraging his great potential.
strengths: Can Silence enemies often by using Discord Strike
Can reposition enemies or himself with Telekinesis
weaknesses: Discord Strike's delay and shape can make it a relatively difficult skillshot

synergies.explanation: Alarak has terrible waveclear, but excels at displacing enemies, while silencing them. Therefore, Assassins with decent waveclear and good damage to follow his combo are excellent with him, such as Jaina or Raynor. E.T.C. and Garrosh are also decent with Alarak, since their displacement and crowdcontrol are good for following his combo, or to setup for it.

counters.explanation: Alarak is countered by crowd control. Johanna and E.T.C. are a threat, since their stuns will not allow Counter-Strike or Telekinesis to be used, turning him into an easy kill. Medivh is also a nuisance, since his Force of Will may protect against Discord Strike, and Poly Bomb is a great follow up to kill you. Deathwing can ignore Alarak, since he is constantly unstoppable and will not be displaced or silenced.

maps.explanation:
Alarak is not able to deal large amounts of damage to non-Heroic entities during PvE encounters with his Abilities; however, he can be effective during team fights that occur during map objectives. He is better on maps that are oriented around team fighting, rather than those that require strong Minion or Mercenary clearing. Narrow choke points can help him land his Abilities on multiple enemy Heroes at the same time.

Alarak is an excellent pick in Battlefield of Eternity, considering he can use Telekinesis to displace enemies into Immortal stun. Be aware this can be done in other maps as well, such as Hanamura Temple, or Tomb of The Spider Queen. You can use it to Displace your enemies into Sentinel's AoE slash, or towards Webweavers' Death Wave.

builds.name: Overwhelming Power Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Alarak's Overwhelming Power Build shifts him from a burst Hero towards a Bruiser playstyle, by enhancing his Basic Attacks, self-sustain, and crowd control. Differently from the other builds, this one does not get Applied Force at Level 7. Therefore, we do not recommend it against poke compositions or against many Ranged Assassins, since you will have a hard time hitting combos or delivering Basic Attacks towards them. Despite this weakness, we find this build excellent when facing melee-heavy team compositions. Alarak will be able to easily punish those melee Heroes, while also reducing their power due to extra Silence or Slow provided by his Level 7 Talents.

Overwhelming Power empowers Basic Attacks and encourages Alarak to be always delivering Basic Attacks after a combo. At Level 7, Hindered Motion is the standard Talent, since it will enable you to be constantly attacking the target, getting value from your Level 1 and 16's Talents. However, if you already have a decent way to reduce your enemy's movements in your team, like Jaina or Fenix provide, we recommend going for Dissonance instead. Lethal Onslaught at Level 16 will be excellent if you have a good amount of Sadism stacks, because it will provide more damage and healing from your Basic Attacks, making it easier to maintain your lead. However, Mocking Strikes will be a great power spike in fights, since it will provide more combos and crowd control for your team.

builds.name: Lightning Surge Build
builds.label: Advanced
builds.description:
The Lightning Surge Build is exceptionally good at long range poke, especially against melee-heavy team compositions. Target enemy Heroes behind the enemy frontline whenever possible, to damage as many Heroes with each cast as possible. When you finish stacking Extended Lightning, you will be able to slow enemies who are hit by the center of the beam. Negatively Charged can be stacked without limit, and is not lost on death. With Hasty Bargain and clever positioning, you can cast Lightning Surge up to 4 times in quick succession. It is very important to focus on hitting enemy Heroes with the center of Lightning Surge's beam, as many of your Talent investments involve this mechanic.

Unfortunately this build has poor early game, and is very reliant on having many stacks from Extended Lightning. For this reason, we only recommend going for it in scenarios where you will easily stack, like in Tomb of the Spider Queen, Braxis Holdout or Infernal Shrines.

builds.name: Combo Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Alarak's Combo Build will enable him to use Telekinesis more often, due to Ruthless Momentum. Show of Force enhances your burst damage, facilitating the kill on the displaced target. It will also be slowly empowering your Sadism, turning Alarak into a real threat. Counter-Strike is a good survivability option for him, however, Deadly Charge can be a good choice for securing kills.

At Level 20, Hasty Bargain is excellent for securing late-game kills. However, if you have chosen Deadly Charge, then Wrath of the Highlord is also a strong choice. On the other hand, with Counter-Strike, it might be more beneficial to stick with Hasty Bargain or consider Might of the Highlord instead.

This build is focused on using Discord Strike and Lightning Surge to follow-up Telekinesis whenever you can do so safely. Do not be afraid to combo Tanks; with a good follow-up, they may lose most of their Health or even get killed by it.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description: Alarak's ARAM build mainly revolves around his Level 4 Talent. ARAM's one-lane nature makes it much easier to stack Negatively Charged. At Level 16, you will start dealing much more damage and will be lethal to most enemies. Therefore, before then, you should focus solely on stacking your quests.

name: Alexstrasza
overview:
Alexstrasza is a Healer who provides raw healing power but does not have access to hard crowd control.

She is particularly efficient if protected by a solid frontline, since she does not have any real escape mechanism.

During important team fights, she uses Dragonqueen to improve her Abilities.
strengths: Relatively low Mana consumption compared to other Healers
Dragonqueen gives a huge advantage during team fights
weaknesses: Weak while Dragonqueen is not available
No access to Cleanse or similar tools to remove crowd-control effects

synergies.explanation:
Alexstrasza has an affinity with Heroes that have high maximum Health (such as Diablo) because Abundance baseline, Life-Binder at Level 10, and Life Unbound at Level 13 provide percent-based healing.

As she lack crowd control, she should be played together with a few Heroes who can provide that (such as Kael'thas thanks to Gravity Lapse), in addition to similar effects provided by the main Tank of your team to peel for her.

counters.explanation:
Alexstrasza offers a lot of raw healing and barely any utility, therefore she struggles against enemey Heroes that have access to healing reduction effects (such as Deckard Cain with Emerald at Level 7).

She suffers against area of effect Abilities (such as Concussion Mine by Junkrat) and/or burst damage (for example Flamestrike by Kael'thas) used on Abundance's location.

Heroes that can stick to Alexstrasza and interrupt (such as Yrel) Dragonqueen and/or Cleansing Flame can put serious pressure on her.

Dragonqueen can be countered by making Alexstrasza unable to act (for example Cocoon by Anub'arak) or by forcing a disengage (like Mighty Gust by Falstad).

maps.explanation:
Alexstrasza heavily prefers Maps that feature a static Objectives with a long cooldown, a single location, and a moderate duration (notably Infernal Shrines) because Dragonqueen can unfold its full potential for a team fight that, if won, will directly translate to taking down a Fort or even a Keep.

The worst Maps for Alexstrasza are the ones where having good sustain healing during the early game is extremely important (in particular Braxis Holdout, but also any other 2-lane Map).

builds.name: Abundance Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Alexstrasza's Abundance Build focuses on area of effect healing and increases your survivability against dives.

Considering that you are spending multiple Talents on Abundance, this Build will be harder to play against area of effect damage and crowd control effects because they can prevent Heroes from benefitting from it.

builds.name: Gift of Life Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Alexstrasza's Gift of Life Build provides high single target sustain healing, regardless of being in combat or not, but it comes online only after unlocking Lifeblossom at Level 7.

The major weakness of this Build is that its healing output goes down when Alexstrasza takes damage, so it should not be played when the enemy team has Heroes who can easily dive her.

builds.name: Flame Buffet Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Alexstrasza's Flame Buffet Build provides good self-sustain to increase your survivability during team fights and massively improves your Dragonqueen in the late game at the cost of healing and early-game power.

Ancient Flame at Level 20 greatly empowers Dragonqueen, allowing you to single-handedly win team fights if the enemy team does not play around it. Slow enemies with Heat Exhaustion at Level 4 and heal yourself with Fire Within at Level 7.

We do not recommend playing this Build on Maps where the early game is important (notably Braxis Holdout) because it provides low sustain healing and needs to scale into the late game.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Alexstrasza's ARAM Build focuses on area of effect healing and increases your survivability against dives.

Considering that you are spending multiple Talents on Abundance, this Build will be harder to play against area of effect damage and crowd control effects because they can prevent Heroes from benefitting from it.

name: Ana
overview: Ana is a Healer who excels at manipulating the course of battle from a safe distance. She is particularly efficient if protected by a solid frontline, since she does not have any real escape mechanism. Consequently, knowing how to position Ana during a team fight is crucial when it comes to staying clear of danger, but also when it comes to healing allied targets from the right angle.
weaknesses: Struggles to heal high-mobility allied Heroes

synergies.explanation:
Nano Boost possesses outstanding synergy with Mages (such as Mephisto) or, more in general, Heroes who deal the majority of their damage with Abilities and not Basic Attacks.

Even if they can also be used on their own, Sleep Dart and Biotic Grenade benefit from allied Heroes who can provide reliable crowd control with their Basic Abilities (like E.T.C.) that will make them impossible to miss.

counters.explanation:
Since her self-healing is limited, Ana usually struggles against Heroes who can ignore her team and dive her instead (such as Chen with Storm, Earth, Fire).

Abilities that can isolate an enemy Hero (like Cocoon by Anub'arak) or disengage (like Mighty Gust by Falstad) can be used to counter Nano Boost in two different ways.

While not as effective as the counters that have been mentioned above, poke is also a decent tool against her, but only if you can actually do considerable damage to her from high distance (such as Hanzo).

There are no Healers who can counter Ana, however, you might prefer going for a Hero who offers utility instead of raw healing (like Lúcio that can count on Sound Barrier to support his team without actually healing them).

maps.explanation: Ana performs better on Maps where the team fight cannot evolve on different fronts because she suffers from flank and dive strategies a lot.

builds.name: Biotic Grenade Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Ana's Biotic Grenade Build increases your healing when allied and/or enemy Heroes tend to group. This usually happens when either team has more than two frontline Heroes or when the enemy team is diving and your team is peeling.

The burst healing from Contact Healing at Level 1 is quite handy when enemy Heroes are on top of you. Anti-Healer at Level 7 helps you hit more Heroes, to get more healing from it. Biotic Enhancements at Level 4 lets you use it more often.

builds.name: Sleep Dart Build
builds.label: Advanced
builds.description:
Ana's Sleep Dart Build improves your offensive tools, to help your team find and secure kills with Sleep Dart, and slightly increases your survivability, by Slowing enemy Heroes and giving you Movement Speed to reposition, dodge, or flee.

Night Terrors at Level 7 adds a considerable amount of percent-based damage on Heroes your team intends to take down. Use it in conjunction with Biotic Grenade to help your team kill even the most durable Heroes (such as Diablo).

builds.name: Shrike Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Ana's Shrike Build is particularly good at trading resources with the enemy team. You can do this by reducing their damage and healing done when affected by Shrike.

The debuff comes from Mind-Numbing Agent at Level 7 and can be applied in two ways: via Basic Attacks, when safe to do so, or via Sleep Dart, thanks to Overdose at Level 4.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Ana's ARAM Build increases your healing when allied and/or enemy Heroes tend to group. This usually happens when either team has more than two frontline Heroes or when the enemy team is diving and your team is peeling.

The burst healing from Contact Healing at Level 1 is quite handy when enemy Heroes are on top of you. Anti-Healer at Level 7 helps you hit more Heroes, to get more healing from it. Biotic Enhancements at Level 4 lets you use it more often.

name: Anduin
overview: Anduin is a ranged Healer that excels at saving his allies, not only by healing them. Notably, Anduin can save allied Heroes in need by using Leap of Faith, which makes them Unstoppable and Pulls them towards Anduin. Mastering Anduin's arsenal of protective and offensive tools provides your team with a powerful Healer in the backline that can contribute a great deal during team fights. Unlike some of the other Healers, Anduin possesses quite some play-making potential utilizing various crowd control and utility effects.

synergies.explanation:
Chastise is not that easy to land, therefore Heroes with reliable crowd control can help Anduin with doing so. For this reason, you should draft Anduin together with a Tank with a Stun, Root, or a powerful Slow. On a similar note, Stitches is a unique Hero who can also help you with that, given you are ready to cast Chastise right after Hook goes off, without waiting to see if it will hit or not, otherwise the projectile will end up being late.

The utility that Anduin offers with Leap of Faith can help allied Heroes who lack mobility (such as Raynor) to get away from danger or even enable more aggressive plays from Heroes that lack escape tools (for example Diablo, to save his Souls).

You can pair Lightbomb with a lot of Abilities (for example Wind Rush by Thrall) to execute powerful and quick engages that the enemy team will struggle to play against or simply use it as a follow-up to other crowd control effects (such as Blessed Shield by Johanna).

counters.explanation:
Anduin cannot rely on Leap of Faith to save allied Heroes from enemy Heroes that can engage multiple times per minute (for example E.T.C. with Powerslide).

A strong dive Hero (such as Sonya) can heavily pressure Anduin, to the point that he will not be able to heal the rest of his team anymore, in addition to rendering Leap of Faith useless.

Poke damage is annoying for Anduin because he lacks area of effect sustain healing to keep everyone healthy during prolonged team fights.

maps.explanation:
Anduin excels on Maps that feature static Objectives where team fights do not last too long (such as Shrines on Dragon Shire). Choke points can make for great locations for Divine Star to get value from as well as to catch enemy Heroes with Lightbomb.

All in all, Anduin's well-rounded kit leaves him with no real Map vulnerabilities, except for a moderate disadvantage on Maps where the Objective takes too much time to be won that his Mana eventually expires (for example Braxis Holdout) and where there are good paths for flanking.

builds.name: Lightwell Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Anduin's Lightwell Build is all about keeping yourself and allied Heroes healthy over time, which is great when facing a team that mostly relies on sustain damage but weak against burst damage.

Try to apply Renew at Level 16 on as many allied Heroes as possible, then rely on Moral Compass to refresh its duration from the distance every 5 seconds with either Divine Star or Basic Attacks.

Most of the Talents in this Build will contribute to reducing the cooldown of Lightwell at Level 1, increasing your healing output without having to spend extra Mana but with the need for allied Heroes to stand in the healing area for a few seconds. For this reason, we find it better for stationary fights to control a given location on the battlefield.

builds.name: Leap of Faith Build
builds.label: Advanced
builds.description:
Anduin's Leap of Faith Build is primarily designed to deal with crowd control and burst damage by sacrificing sustain healing.

Desperate Prayer at Level 7 provides burst healing, and Glyph of Faith at Level 16 gives you another charge of Leap of Faith to save allied Heroes from danger.

builds.name: Inner Focus Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Anduin's Inner Focus Build is designed to help you stay alive against dive (for example Zeratul) as otherwise you do not have tools to deal with it.

The survivability comes from Blessed Recovery at Level 7 and Inner Focus at Level 16, whose cooldown is reduced by dealing damage to enemy Heroes. Varian's Legacy at Level 20 also helps with that.

builds.label: ARAM

Anduin's ARAM Build is all about keeping yourself and allied Heroes healthy over time, which is great when facing a team that mostly relies on sustain damage but weak against burst damage.

name: Anub'arak
overview: Anub'arak is an aggressive anti-caster Tank. His strongest points are his long-range disruption and powerful on-demand resistance to Ability-based damage. Although considered an archetypal Tank, Anub'arak's Health pool is considerably lower than that of other Tanks. He relies on opportunism and teamwork to survive, exemplifying the adage "the best defence is a good offence."
strengths: Access to Cocoon, a valuable Heroic Ability
weaknesses: Main Abilities are skillshots that can be avoided

synergies.explanation: Anub'arak's aggressive crowd control-oriented Ability set makes him particularly useful to any Hero who is able to follow up on said crowd control with their own Ability combo.

counters.explanation: Anub'arak's aggressive game plan is difficult to execute against Heroes that have ways of avoiding his skillshot or becoming immune to crowd control on-demand.

maps.explanation:
Anub'arak can be played without major issues on most Maps because he has access to powerful engage and peeling tools.

His best Map is Alterac Pass because, by using his Trait to keep Guards busy, he can capture the enemy Objective all by himself as long as the enemy Heroes are busy somewhere else.

Maps where aggressive plays are rewarded (notably Dragon Shire) are great for Anub'arak because, when the enemy team is split into small groups, he can make high-risk high-reward plays to gain an advantage.

He does not excel on Maps where the Tank has to posture in vision for long (for example Braxis Holdout) because Anub'arak is not that durable against Basic Attacks or where those Heroes are popular.

builds.name: Beetles Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Anub'arak's Beetles Build increases his sustain damage and self-sustain during prolonged team fights and when pushing. In the mid game you also gain some waveclear.

The increased damage and waveclear mainly come from Burning Beetles at Level 13. The survivability comes from Leeching Scarabs at Level 7 and potentially from Legion of Beetles at Level 1 blocking skillshots.

Last but not the least, Legion of Beetles at Level 1 spawns additional Beetles and makes them harder to kill, allowing you to get more value from the rest of the Build.

builds.name: Burrow Charge Build
builds.label: Advanced
builds.description:
Anub'arak's Burrow Charge Build increases his burst damage, range, and survivability while using Burrow Charge aggressively, either immediately after Impale hits an enemy Hero or from over impassable terrain to take opponents off guard.

The survivability mostly comes from Subterranean Shield at Level 7 and the damage comes from Urticating Spines at Level 13, which is the best option when it comes to burst damage.

builds.name: Harden Carapace Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Anub'arak's Harden Carapace Build increases his mobility to reposition in team fights and dodge skillshots, burst damage to secure kills, and survivability against Spell Damage.

Consider going for this Build when playing against Heroes who can deal Spell Damage with high tick rate (like Tassadar) or as damage over time (such as Lunara). This will trigger Chitinous Plating at Level 7 and thus allow you to get more value from Harden Carapace-related Talent.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Anub'arak's ARAM Build increases his sustain damage and self-sustain during prolonged team fights and when pushing. In the mid game you also gain some waveclear.

The increased damage and waveclear mainly come from Burning Beetles at Level 13. The survivability comes from Leeching Scarabs at Level 7 and potentially from Legion of Beetles at Level 1 blocking skillshots.

Last but not the least, Legion of Beetles at Level 1 spawns additional Beetles and makes them harder to kill, allowing you to get more value from the rest of the Build.

name: Artanis
overview: Artanis is an aggressive Bruiser that excels at fighting for prolonged periods of time thanks to Shield Overload and its related Talents making him difficult to kill without the use of crowd control and burst damage together.
strengths: Phase Prism can be used during Blade Dash to pull enemy Heroes
Shield Overload can make Artanis difficult to kill using sustain damage only
Heroic Abilities with unlimited range, allowing him to contribute to team fights on the other side of the battlefield
weaknesses: Crowd control can prevent Artanis from using his Basic Attacks and/or Abilities, making him unable to reduce the cooldown of Shield Overload

synergies.explanation: Artanis pairs extremely well with Healers who can provide sustained healing (such as Malfurion) to gradually replenish his Health while his own Shields guarantee him protection against burst damage, with Heroes who can crowd control enemy Heroes to either keep them at melee distance (for example Arthas with his Root or even just his Slow) or to stop them in place after a successful Blade Dash plus Phase Prism combo (like Kael'thas with Gravity Lapse), and Heroes who can mitigate his lack of mobility (such as Zarya with Speed Barrier at Level 4).

counters.explanation: Artanis gets countered by Heroes who can Knockback him out of his Blade Dash's animation (such as E.T.C. with Face Melt), Heroes who can Root him or even just Slow him (for example Arthas and Lunara respectively), Heroes who can Blind him (such as Johanna with Shield Glare), and Heroes who can deal bonus damage to Shields (Varian with Shattering Throw comes to mind).

maps.explanation: Artanis is good on Maps where he can get value from Amateur Opponent at Level 1 to take down a big Monster at the Objective (such as the Immortal on Battlefield of Eternity) or for a strong Mercenary Camp (for example the Sentinel on Hanamura Temple) but he suffers on Maps where it is important that the Offlaner has waveclear (such as Towers of Doom).

builds.name: Blade Dash Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Artanis's Blade Dash Build is designed to heavily increase your survivability by empowering Shield Overload as much as possible, indirectly helping you to deal more damage over the course of a team fight.

The combination of Shield Battery at Level 4, Templar's Zeal at Level 13, and Force of Will at Level 16 makes Artanis hard to take down even when countered by Blinds.

Level 13 can be either Phase Bulwark against burst damage or Templar's Zeal against sustain damage.

builds.name: Phase Prism Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Artanis's Phase Prism Build provides various buffs when you hit enemy Heroes with Phase Prism: Armor, Attack Speed, and cooldown reduction.

Chrono Surge at Level 7 and Blades of a Templar at Level 16 give you Attack Speed that helps you stack Protector Of Aiur at Level 1, slowly turning you into a late-game powerhouse.

builds.name: Twin Blades Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Artanis's Twin Blades Build is designed to give you a high amount of damage, mostly in the form of burst damage right after activating Twin Blades.

You should consider this Build only if you really want to take down high-mobility Heroes who are diving in the backline of your team or if you need percent-based damage.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Artanis's ARAM Build provides various buffs when you hit enemy Heroes with Phase Prism: Armor, Attack Speed, and cooldown reduction.

Chrono Surge at Level 7 and Blades of a Templar at Level 16 give you Attack Speed that helps you stack Protector Of Aiur at Level 1, slowly turning you into a late-game powerhouse.

name: Arthas
overview: Arthas is a Tank who relies on Roots and Slows to peel for his team or to stop enemy Heroes from retreating. This type of crowd-control is great against melee Heroes that rely on Basic Attacks and lack mobility.
strengths: Counters melee Heroes that rely on Basic Attacks
weaknesses: Consumes a lot of Mana with Frozen Tempest

synergies.explanation:
Arthas pairs well with Heroes who can either follow-up on his crowd control (such as Chromie with A Proper Greeting) or initiate with their own (for example Maiev), especially if your main Tank does not provide enough crowd control for peeling (Stitches comes to mind).

Heroes who can give him some mobility (for example Zarya with Speed Barrier at Level 4) and/or help him survive through burst damage definitely help (such as Medivh).

counters.explanation:
Arthas, due to his lack of mobility gets easily countered by Displacement effects (such as Wrecking Ball by Garrosh).

He also suffers against burst damage usually coming from Mages (for example Kel'Thuzad), healing reduction effects (such as Emerald by Deckard Cain), high range (Hanzo comes to mind), Slow effects (for example Jaina), and high mobility (such as Zeratul played correctly).

maps.explanation:
Due to Frozen Tempest being heavy on Mana consumption, Arthas suffers on Maps where he needs to stay active for long periods of time (with Braxis Holdout being the major offender) and does not shine on Maps where it is highly preferred to have your Offlaner take care of 2 lanes by double soaking (for example top-mid on Towers of Doom).

While being decent at it, Arthas does not excel at capturing Camps and/or defending enemy Mercenaries in lane, making him a suboptimal pick on Maps where macro is important (for example Garden of Terror).

builds.name: Death Coil Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Arthas's Death Coil Build is designed to increase his damage from the distance, his team's burst damage, and his self-sustain. We find this Build particularly good against ranged Heroes.

Frost Presence at Level 1 makes both your engage and your peeling reliable. The burst damage comes from Shattered Armor at Level 4 and Deathlord at Level 13.

When playing against Heroes with slow but heavy hitting Basic Attacks, pick Rime at Level 1. When playing against Heroes who deal a lot of damage with Abilities, pick Anti-Magic Shell at Level 16.

builds.name: Howling Blast Build
builds.label: Advanced
builds.description:
Arthas's Howling Blast Build is designed to increase his damage from the distance, his team's burst damage, and his survivability against burst damage. We find this Build particularly good for short team fights.

Frost Presence at Level 1 makes both your engage and your peeling reliable. The burst damage comes from Shattered Armor at Level 4 and Deathchill at Level 13.

When playing against Heroes with slow but heavy hitting Basic Attacks, pick Rime at Level 1. When playing against Heroes who deal a lot of damage with Abilities, pick Anti-Magic Shell at Level 16.

builds.name: Frozen Tempest Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Arthas's Frozen Tempest Build allows him to cripple the enemy team's advance or retreat by further increasing the power and utility of Frozen Tempest. We find this Build particularly good against melee Heroes with low-mobility.

Borean Winds at Level 1 gives a moderate amount of mobility, Biting Cold at Level 13 increases your damage output, and Remorseless Winter at Level 16 provides another way to Root enemy Heroes.

When playing against Heroes with slow but heavy hitting Basic Attacks, pick Rime at Level 1. When playing against Heroes who deal a lot of damage with Abilities, pick Anti-Magic Shell at Level 16.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Arthas's ARAM Build is designed to increase his damage from the distance, his team's burst damage, and his self-sustain. We find this Build particularly good against ranged Heroes.

Frost Presence at Level 1 makes both your engage and your peeling reliable. The burst damage comes from Shattered Armor at Level 4 and Deathlord at Level 13.

When playing against Heroes with slow but heavy hitting Basic Attacks, pick Rime at Level 1. When playing against Heroes who deal a lot of damage with Abilities, pick Anti-Magic Shell at Level 16.

name: Auriel
overview: Auriel is a Healer who turns part of the damage done by a chosen allied Hero and by herself into area of effect healing.
strengths: High sustain healing during team fights
Strong crowd control near impassable terrain
weaknesses: Low sustain healing when out of combat
Heroic Abilities that make the target allied Hero's position exploitable
No access to Cleanse or similar tools to remove crowd-control effects

synergies.explanation:
To get the most value out of Bestow Hope, you should pick Auriel together with a Hero who can consistently deal damage from the distance (such as Valla) without relying too much on skillshots.

Detainment Strike benefits from impassable terrain, making Auriel better when paired with Heroes that can push enemy Heroes on it (like Diablo with Shadow Charge) or create it out of nowhere (for example Nazeebo with Zombie Wall).

As she can fight for long periods of time without having Mana issues, Auriel likes to be in team with Heroes who can take care of multiple lanes at the same time by double soaking (like Yrel) while the rest of her team puts a lot of pressure on a single lane.

Since she heals using Energy instead of Mana, Auriel is one of the best Healers to pair with Cho'Gall, another Hero without Mana. Furthermore, using Bestow Hope on them will convert both Cho's and Gall's damage into Energy.

counters.explanation:
The 4-second cooldown on Ray of Heaven prevents it from saving allied Heroes from burst damage. A well-timed crowd control (such as Wailing Arrow) 3 seconds after she cast the previous Ray of Heaven can further extend this time frame.

Heroes who have access to Knockback effects (like Junkrat with Concussion Mine) can use them to split Auriel's team so that she cannot use Ray of Heaven on multiple Heroes at the same time.

Auriel's Heroic Abilities allows the enemy team to easily follow up with their Abilities (for example Entangling Roots by Malfurion).

Due to her dependency on dealing damage to get Energy for healing, Auriel does not perform that well against poke damage (such as Hanzo), especially when the enemy team has the lead.

maps.explanation:
The fact that Auriel does not use Mana is great during the early game, therefore she is a fantastic pick on Maps where a good start can make the difference between a win and a loss (notably Braxis Holdout).

If your team has an Offlaner who can double soak (such as Xul), you can basically play Auriel on 3-lane Maps like when you are playing on 2-lane Maps, so just focus on a side lane and pressure the enemy team as much as you can.

Auriel also likes Maps where she can exploit impassable terrain to Stun enemy Heroes with Detainment Strike.

builds.name: Detainment Strike Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Auriel's Detainment Strike Build empowers your healing output, crowd control, and damage. Due to how Detainment Strike works, this Build works best when fighting near impassable terrain.

Level 13 is flexible. You can pick Blinding Flash to Blind melee Heroes, Converging Force as a secondary interrupt for stationary channels, or Piercing Lash to for additional crowd control on grouped enemy Heroes.

Since it increases your maximum Energy, Reservoir of Hope at Level 16 not only makes Ray of Heaven heal more but also deal more damage to enemy Heroes via Searing Light at Level 1. So, when hitting enemy Heroes with it, you will gain Energy.

builds.name: Sacred Sweep Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Auriel's Sacred Sweep Build empowers your healing output and damage on grouped enemy Heroes who cannot punish you. Due to how Sacred Sweep works, this Build works best when facing at least 3 melee Heroes and when the enemy team lacks crowd control effects.

The increased radius provided by Majestic Span at Level 4 makes it easier to hit enemy Heroes with Sacred Sweep, which is great for Righteous Assault at Level 1 and Converging Force at Level 13.

Since it increases your maximum Energy, Reservoir of Hope at Level 16 not only makes Ray of Heaven heal more but also deal more damage to enemy Heroes via Searing Light at Level 1. So, when hitting enemy Heroes with it, you will gain Energy.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Auriel's ARAM Build empowers your healing output, crowd control, and damage. Due to how Detainment Strike works, this Build works best when fighting near impassable terrain.

Level 13 is flexible. You can pick Blinding Flash to Blind melee Heroes, Converging Force as a secondary interrupt for stationary channels, or Piercing Lash to for additional crowd control on grouped enemy Heroes.

Since it increases your maximum Energy, Reservoir of Hope at Level 16 not only makes Ray of Heaven heal more but also deal more damage to enemy Heroes via Searing Light at Level 1. So, when hitting enemy Heroes with it, you will gain Energy.

name: Azmodan
overview: Azmodan is a caster that revels in long-range assaults and sieging. Defined by his abnormally large Health pool and Globe of Annihilation Ability, Azmodan is able to scale his damage output beyond that of most other Heroes. As a tradeoff, he has very limited options for crowd control and mobility.
strengths: High area of effect damage output potential and waveclear
Outstanding survivability for a Ranged Assassin
Excellent sieger, particularly when left alone
weaknesses: Large and relatively immobile; easy to body block
Limited team fight utility beyond raw damage; no crowd control

synergies.explanation: Azmodan's dependency on stacking up Annihilation makes him particularly effective with Heroes that can "cook up" Minion waves for him to last-hit. Otherwise, he works well with anyone that provides reliable crowd control, particularly over an area of effect. Since Azmodan's early-game presence tends to be limited, avoid picking him along other lacklustre early-game Heroes such as Abathur or Murky.

counters.explanation: Given his reliance upon channeling, as both Globe of Annihilation and All Shall Burn are put on a full Cooldown after interruption, Azmodan is naturally countered by Heroes that provide reliable means of Stunning or Silencing him. His tendency to split push also leaves him vulnerable to aggressive gankers, especially due to his large collision that makes him easy to hit and body block.

maps.explanation: Azmodan revels on Maps that are either very large or very small; this is due to his broadly different play styles. Small, three-Lane Maps are generally good for Annihilation stacking, whereas larger Maps promote split pushing styles. Regardless, Azmodan can work on most Maps, granted you adapt your strategy.

builds.name: Greed Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description: The Greed build focuses primarily on split pushing through the use of Azmodan's minions and heroic ability. Demonic Invasion does significant siege damage and can be used behind turrets directly onto a keep or fort and can slowly demolish them throughout the game. With the talents buffing Azmodan's All Shall Burn, he can provide some good teamfight presence as well.

builds.name: Gluttony Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description: The Gluttony exploits the synergy between the aforementioned Talent, Art of Chaos, Total Annihilation, and Inescapable Annihilation, which are notable for making Globe of Annihilation powerful at all stages of the game. The rest of the build seeks to improves Summon Demon Warrior. Although inherently weak, Demon Warriors become significantly more useful with the key Hellforged Armor and Brutish Vanguard Talents.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description: Azmodan's ARAM build is similar to the Gluttony Build and sees no changes in terms of playstyle. Spam Globe of Annhilation until you win the game.

name: Blaze
overview: Blaze is a heavy Tank with great waveclear, powerful crowd-control, and high survivability thanks to his large Health pool and dependable self-sustain. Due to Jet Propulsion having a long delay, Blaze is not good against high-mobility Heroes (for example Tracer) and ideally requires other Heroes to start the engage for him.
strengths: Outstanding ability to disrupt opponents' plans through plentiful crowd control and Bunker Drop
Hard to kill due to large Health pool and on-demand access to Armor
Respectable area of effect damage potential and waveclear for a Tank
weaknesses: Reliance on multiple skillshots that can be avoided
Fairly immobile, thus prone to be kited
Limited burst and single-target damage output

synergies.explanation: Blaze's well-rounded Ability set allows him to work in most team compositions and with most other Heroes, granted he is also picked for his anti-melee role. Oil Spill's Slowing effect is particularly useful for improving the uptime of Assassins, whereas most Heroes with skillshots will find Jet Propulsion a great way of setting up for accurate hits.

counters.explanation: Since Blaze relies on skillshots to deal damage and on the rather slow charge up of Jet Propulsion to initiate, he tends to struggle offensively against highly mobile Heroes. Furthermore, his large Health pool and limited mobility makes him particularly vulnerable to percentage-based damage.

maps.explanation:
Thanks to his great waveclear and good self-sustain, Blaze excels on Maps where it is possible to double-soak and does well on most Maps.

Blaze can get a lot of value from his Abilities on Maps that feature static Objectives that force opponents to fight within a specific area or in enclosed spaces (such as Infernal Shrines).

On the contrary, Blaze does not excel at dueling, therefore he does not do well on Maps where there is a Capture Point to contest in the early game (so Braxis Holdout).

builds.name: Basic Attacks Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Blaze's Basic Attacks Build primarily empowers your waveclear while also increasing your survivability, utility, and damage. As a consequence, we recommend this Build when playing Blaze as Offlaner.

In particular, Incinerator Gauntlets at Level 4 makes it easier to clear Minions and Mercenaries while laning and Adrenaline Stimpack at Level 1 further empowers its value against Mercenaries while also boosting your damage against enemy Heroes.

builds.name: Oil Spill Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Blaze's Oil Spill Build primarily empowers your engage while also increasing your survivability, utility, and damage. We recommend this Build when playing Blaze as Tank, preferably against 2 melee Heroes or less.

In particular, the Slow increase provided by Oil Dispersal at Level 4 makes it easier to use Oil Spill as a setup for Jet Propulsion.

builds.name: Pyromania Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Blaze's Pyromania Build primarily empowers your engage while also increasing your survivability, utility, and damage. We recommend this Build when playing Blaze as Tank, ideally against 3 melee Heroes or more.

In particular, the damage reduction from Meltdown at Level 4 is great for reducing the damage done by melee Heroes and Heat Treatment at Level 16 can heal you by a lot when surrounded by enemy Heroes in melee range. The cooldown reduction from New Habits at Level 1 lets you do this more often.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Blaze's ARAM Build primarily empowers your engage while also increasing your survivability, utility, and damage. As a consequence, we recommend this Build when playing Blaze as Tank.

In particular, the Slow increase provided by Oil Dispersal at Level 4 makes it easier to use Oil Spill as a setup for Jet Propulsion.

name: Brightwing
overview: Brightwing is a ranged Healer with strong global presence. She is capable of continually healing nearby allies without using Mana and protect them against enemy crowd control effects, due to her Soothing Mist Trait. Her ability to teleport to an allied Hero across the entire map makes Brightwing a very mobile Hero that excels on large battlegrounds, like Cursed Hollow.
strengths: Soothing Mist does not require any Mana
Strong disengage thanks to Emerald Wind
Built-in Cleanse that breaks Stuns, Slows, Roots, and Silences every 75 seconds
Allows a variety of talent builds depending on the game situation
weaknesses: Requires a lot of map awareness
Her burst or sustained healing takes time or channeling to be applied
Fairly high skill cap compared to other Healers

synergies.explanation: Since Brightwing's Phase Shift heals based on the target's maximum Health, she is excellent with high-health Heroes, like Diablo, Stitches, or Cho. Furthermore, through her global mobility she provides good support for dives, being a good pick with Heroes that excel at that, like Genji or Tracer.

counters.explanation: Brightwing gets countered by crowd control heavy Tanks that cannot have their engages canceled by Polymorph, such as Anub'arak, Johanna, or E.T.C..

maps.explanation: Brightwing does particularly well on larger Maps like Towers of Doom or Warhead Junction, on which she can use her global mobility to great effect. On rotation-heavy maps like Tomb of the Spider Queen, Brightwing's inability to use a mount can often slow her down, making her a liability against aggressive pushing compositions.

builds.name: Critical Mist Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description: Brightwing's Critical Mist Build, thanks to Critical Mist, focuses on denying crowd control engages from enemies while providing good healing for your team. It is a great option against compositions with many different area of effect Stuns (like Blaze and E.T.C. have) or Roots.

builds.name: Teleport Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Brightwing's Teleport Build focuses on providing great global mobility, which becomes particularly useful on larger Maps like Cursed Hollow, Garden of Terror, or the medium-sized Infernal Shrines.

At Level 16, we mention Critterize as the main Talent, since it will greatly enhance Brightwing's capabilities to kill any targeted Hero. However, Hush! is a great option if your team is more focused on dealing sustain damage, instead of on blowing up a target. Phase Out is not necessary, but is an option if you are being the target very often.

builds.name: Arcane Flare Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description: The Arcane Flare Build emphasizes Brightwing's unexpectedly strong damage and crowd control when combining several Q-based talents such as Dream Shot at Level 4, Sticky Flare at Level 7, and Hush! at Level 16. Phase Out can be a helpful defensive talent to pick up at Level 16, since casting Blink Heal may sometimes cause Brightwing to get too close to the enemy team.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description: Brightwing's ARAM Build takes advantage of your team being grouped at all times, allowing you to consistently heal everyone with Critical Mist's activation.

name: Cassia
overview: Cassia is a ranged Assassin who deals increased damage to Blinded enemies. Blinding Light makes her exceptionally strong against melee Heroes who are reliant on Basic Attacks as a primary damage source. Although she has strong all-in potential with Ball Lightning and Fend, her kit lacks escape options once she is committed. While Cassia can fit into many different team compositions, she gets very squishy when against crowd control.
strengths: Decent waveclear with Fend if Minions are Blinded
Great against melee Heroes due to Charged Strikes
Strong against Basic Attack oriented Heroes thanks to Blinding Light
Gets more value from Healing, due to having innate armor from Avoidance
weaknesses: Any debuff that stops movement will greatly reduce her survivability

synergies.explanation: Cassia greatly benefits from allied Heroes who can Blind enemies, because she deals increased damage to Blinded targets. If her allies can also Slow enemies, she can get additional value from Martial Law.

counters.explanation: Cassia has no escapes, limited self-sustain and small range. Powerful backline Heroes can win trades with her at range, and punish her brutally if she dives in with Fend. Reliable crowd controls are also excellent against her, since Avoidance is only active when Cassia is moving.

maps.explanation: Cassia can perform well on any map. She has good waveclear, excellent siege damage at gates, is an effective duelist, and contributes high single-target damage against Boss type map objectives. Her viability is more dependent on team compositions than battlegrounds.

builds.name: Lightning Fury Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
This Build slightly increases Lightning Fury's damage, and is a great option if you are looking for more poke damage. The playstyle of this build differs greatly from the other builds, as you will usually deal damage from a safer range.

Use Lightning Fury on enemy Heroes whenever possible, in order to stack Thunderstroke quickly. If you cast Lightning Fury perpendicularly toward enemy Gates, the lightning bolts will also damage the Towers and Walls with each cast.

builds.name: Charged Strikes Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Cassia's Charged Strikes Build will make you deal a substantial amount of sustain damage through Basic Attacks to the enemy team. The main drawback of this build is that it requires you to remain within Cassia's short attack range while delivering Basic Attacks. But this weakness is compensated by Gloves Of Alacrity at Level 13.

Due to Cassia's small range, you will have a hard time constantly delivering Basic Attacks in the early game. It is better to be playing safely, only attacking enemies when you are sure of your safety. Start playing more aggressively after Level 13's Talents, because of the extra range or mobility provided by those.

source.author_line: Last updated on May 31, 2025 at 10:00 by Derenash

name: Chen
overview: Chen is a durable Bruiser and a strong duelist as he can trade exceptionally well against many Heroes thanks to his solid damage output and high self-sustain, making him one of the best Offlaners in the game when played correctly.
strengths: Solid damage output, especially against Heroes

synergies.explanation: Chen likes to play together with Heroes that can empower his dive (such as Tyrael), dive with him (for example Abathur), provide waveclear (like Rehgar), clear Mercenary Camps (for example Greymane), and/or offer crowd control (such as Johanna).

counters.explanation:
Whether team fighting or dueling, Chen struggles against Heroes who have access to crowd control effects that can interrupt Fortifying Brew (for example E.T.C. with either Powerslide or Face Melt) because, without channeling it for at least 1 second due to a quick interrupt, he will not have enough Brew to use some of his Basic Abilities.

Speaking about team fights in particular, anything that can protect his target from a dive attempt makes Chen's plan more difficult to execute (for example a well-timed Sanctification by Tyrael or even a Sound Barrier by Lúcio).

If we consider the macro aspect of the game, primarily due to his low waveclear, Chen has a hard time when the enemy team has access to Heroes who can completely warp the game and allow the enemy team to play in a different way than usual (such as Abathur and The Lost Vikings).

maps.explanation:
Chen performs better on Maps where he needs to take care of a single lane, the Boss Camp is a strong win condition, and macro is not that important.

Due to his mediocre waveclear, Chen is not that good on Maps where double soaking is important (such as Towers of Doom), even if he can still provide good value in team fights thanks to his Heroic Abilities.

Chen does not excel on big Maps (like Garden of Terror) because, when it comes to macro, he cannot compete with Heroes who can quickly clear Minions or do Mercenary Camps alone.

builds.name: Hybrid Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Chen's Hybrid Build focus on increasing your damage as much as possible, mostly by empowering Abilities. Paired with Chen's good survivability, the additional damage allows you to take down valuable enemy Heroes with little to no help from your team.

Accumulating Flame at Level 1 progressively increases your damage output during the game and, more importantly, your waveclear. In order to get more stacks, remember to hit enemy Heroes whenever it is safe to do so.

Withering Flames at Level 4 allows you to trade better with enemy Heroes without getting in melee range. A Touch of Honey at Level 13 helps you engage or stick on enemy Heroes.

builds.name: Flying Kick Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Chen's Flying Kick Build is designed to keep your damage high when you cannot rely on Basic Attacks that much, either because you are countered by enemy Heroes or because team fights will be relatively short, and a lot of playmaking potential via Wandering Keg.

After picking Enough to Share at Level 13, briefly using Fortifying Brew to get a Shield and stopping as soon as possible becomes a valid play to trigger the bonus damage of Deadly Strike at Level 4.

Flying Kick will deal more damage thanks to Deadly Strike at Level 4. Tap Fortifying Brew right before using Flying Kick to deal even more damage thanks to Enough to Share at Level 13 instantly giving you a Shield.

builds.name: Stagger Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Chen's Stagger Build focuses on increasing your survivability by making Stagger more efficient and boosting your damage output by empowering your Basic Attacks and Breath of Fire.

Accumulating Flame at Level 1 progressively increases your damage output during the game and, more importantly, your waveclear. In order to get more stacks, remember to hit enemy Heroes whenever it is safe to do so.

Combined together, Gift of the Ox at Level 7 and Celerity at Level 16 make Chen harder to kill. The latter can reduce Stagger's cooldown, which makes you get more value from both Talents.

Withering Flames at Level 4 allows you to trade better with enemy Heroes without getting in melee range. A Touch of Honey at Level 13 helps you engage or stick on enemy Heroes.

builds.name: Basic Attacks Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Chen's Basic Attacks Build focus on increasing your damage as much as possible, mostly by empowering Basic Attacks. Paired with Chen's good survivability, the additional damage allows you to take down valuable enemy Heroes with little to no help from your team.

Accumulating Flame at Level 1 progressively increases your damage output during the game and, more importantly, your waveclear. In order to get more stacks, remember to hit enemy Heroes whenever it is safe to do so.

Combo Strikes at Level 16 is the signature Talent of this Build, heavily increasing your damage output especially when paired with Eye of the Tiger at Level 4 for even more damage from Basic Attacks against enemy Heroes.

Eye of the Tiger at Level 4 allows you to trade better with enemy Heroes while in melee range. A Touch of Honey at Level 13 helps you engage or stick on enemy Heroes.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Chen's ARAM Build focus on increasing your damage as much as possible, mostly by empowering Abilities. Paired with Chen's good survivability, the additional damage allows you to take down valuable enemy Heroes with little to no help from your team.

Accumulating Flame at Level 1 progressively increases your damage output during the game and, more importantly, your waveclear. In order to get more stacks, remember to hit enemy Heroes whenever it is safe to do so.

Withering Flames at Level 4 allows you to trade better with enemy Heroes without getting in melee range. A Touch of Honey at Level 13 helps you engage or stick on enemy Heroes.

name: Cho
overview:
Cho is half of the entity controlled by two players known as Cho'gall. The player in charge of Cho has the burden of controlling the entity's movement and Basic Attacks, whereas the second player, in control of Gall, acts as a "turret" that uses Abilities from Cho's physical position. Cho's strongest points are his area of effect disruption, outstanding resilience, and ability to safely position Gall, whom can deal high levels of sustain damage, right into the midst of combat. Should Cho be killed, Gall will die with him, instantly yielding two kills worth of Experience to opponents.

Given the highly unusual nature of Cho, we highly recommend that you use this guide along with our guide for Gall, so as to get a better understanding of the Hero.
strengths: Permanently tied to Gall, an Assassin, making coordination easy
Strongest late game in Heroes of the Storm
Provides vision for his team with Eye of Kilrogg
weaknesses: Deaths are twice as punishing, as they mean losing two Heroes
Only allows a team to have 4 Heroes, reducing overall Map presence
Very reliant on Heroic Abilities to significantly impact team fights

synergies.explanation: Cho'gall's nature makes him thrive when teamed up with a strong Healer, particularly those who possesses great single target healing, like Alexstrasza's Life-Binder, Brightwing's Phase Shift, or Ana's constant Healing. Furthermore, a good bruiser or tank to be with Cho in the frontline is a great addition to the composition.

counters.explanation: Cho'gall's nature makes him particularly vulnerable to most forms of crowd control, strong single-target damage, and percent-based damage sources. Fortunately, Cho'gall has plenty of Talent choices and maneuvers that allow him to adapt to a variety of less-than-ideal situations. However, Anub'arak's Cocoon or Maiev's Containment Disc can turn the fight into a 5v3, and are a major threat to Cho'gall.

maps.explanation: Since Cho'gall is completely dependent on late game Talents, he excels on maps which will mostly reach Levels 16 and 20. He is extremely weak in snowball maps, like Battlefield of Eternity and Warhead Junction.

builds.name: Standard Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
This standard build provides a balance between sustain and mobility. Calloused Hide greatly enhance Cho's teamfighting potential and escape capabilities when he is low on health, being a great Talent for surviving through the early game.

Like all the Cho and Gall builds, it has great power spikes at Level 13 and beyond. At this Level, Twilight Veil is the standard Talent, but Surging Dash is decent against poke compositions, while Molten Block is good against burst percent-based damage that armor cannot be reduced (such as Greymane's Cursed Bullet and Malthael's Last Rites).

builds.name: Basic Attacks Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Cho's Basic Attacks build is totally focused on constantly delivering Basic Attacks against enemy Heroes. Since it has Consuming Fire and Firestarter, this build will be incredibly strong if you can keep hitting enemies, but falls behind other options when enemies can punish you during the early game.

A good point to note is that with this build, you can deal good damage while tanking, with either Ogre Hide or Twilight Veil to protect yourself.

builds.name: Surging Fist Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Uppercut adds good percentage damage and insane mobility to Cho. Being able to cast Surging Fist again after hitting 2 targets with it can turn the tides of a fight easily. However, it can be easily canceled by any crowd control, greatly reducing this build's effectiveness. For this reason, we recommend going for this Build when enemies do not have many ways to cancel Surging Fist and if they do, it is better to wait for it to be wasted to cast the Ability again.

Since you do not get Seared Flesh at Level 4, attack speed will not be a great addition at Level 16, so Runed Gauntlet is a better choice at that tier.

name: Chromie
overview: Chromie is a Ranged Assassin with outstanding burst damage and poke potential. Her strong burst Abilities allow her to inflict heavy damage onto her targets, while both of her Heroic Abilities provide her with decent crowd control during team fights. When playing Chromie, it is of utmost importance to anticipate your target's movement path, since both Sand Blast and Dragon's Breath come with a short delay. Ultimately, Chromie is a Hero that requires good game sense and quick reflexes in order to shine, however, if played well, she is one of the most dangerous Ranged Assassins in the game.
strengths: Both Slowing Sands and Temporal Loop are viable Heroic Abilities

synergies.explanation: One of Chromie's favorite Healers has to be Malfurion. His Innervate Trait provides her with precious Mana regeneration and cooldown reduction, while his Regrowth allows Chromie to stay in battle for a long period of time. Another Healer that works wonders with Chromie is Ana, whose Nano Boost greatly empowers Chromie's damage for a short period of time.

counters.explanation: Chromie struggles against two kinds of Heroes: the ones that are too beefy for her to take down quickly and the ones that are too fast for her to reliably land her Basic Abilities. As such, Heroes like Illidan or Tracer can become quite dangerous.

maps.explanation: Chromie performs decent on most maps. Her current best maps are Volskaya Foundry and Braxis Holdout. This is due to the nature of the maps allowing her to poke into the objective zone. Chromie does not really have any weak maps as her poke is a threat on any map where there is an objective area both teams need to be on.

builds.name: Sand Blast Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description: Chromie’s Sand Blast build focuses on maximizing her long-range poke and burst damage. The build enhances Sand Blast, allowing Chromie to consistently pressure enemies from a safe distance. It’s especially strong when you can land your shots reliably, making positioning and accuracy the key to getting the most out of the build.

builds.name: Dragon's Breath Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description: The Dragon's Breath build focuses on enhancing Chromie's Dragon's Breath ability. Through Deep Breathing, Chromie can significantly increase the damage output. The build heavily relies on hitting enemy heroes in the center of your Dragon's Breath, therefore, having CC on your team and waiting for them to use their abilities will greatly improve your own damage output. Thanks to the slow from Mobius Loop, hitting an enemy hero with the first wave can increase the chance of them getting hit by all three.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description: Chromie's ARAM build is similar to the Dragon's Breath Build, and due to Chromie's passive ability, you unlock her power spike quite early in ARAM games. Infinite stacking proves to be quite strong and becomes even stronger if games last longer.

name: Deathwing
overview:
Deathwing is a melee Bruiser with various ranged Abilities that also make him a threat to be reckoned with from larger distances. His massive dragon form renders him resistant to enemy crowd control, however, it also prevents any form of healing or Shielding on him.

He excels at dealing dangerous burst damage onto his foes, however, most of his Abilities have a rather slow casting animation, allowing most opponents to dodge them if they are not impaired in their movement. Thus, Deathwing is a heavy hitter that is somewhat reliant on his teammates to pave the way for his impactful damage Abilities by using crowd control effects on enemy Heroes.
strengths: Immune to any form of crowd control
Great at pushing and sieging enemy Structures
weaknesses: Cannot be affected by allies' buffs or healing

synergies.explanation: It is hard to find Heroes that naturally synergize with Deathwing, since he cannot be buffed or enhanced in any way. However, there are some Heroes, usually crowd control heavy Tanks, that can make it easier for Deathwing to land his devastating damage Abilities. Consequently, we find Heroes like E.T.C., Johanna, or Arthas to be a fitting match, since their Stuns and Slows can buy enough time for Deathwing to wipe the opposing team off the battlefield.

counters.explanation: Because of Deathwing's health, size, and low mobility, there are two types of Heroes that counter him very well. Firstly, percentage-based damage abilities, such as Tychus' Minigun or Greymane's Cursed Bullet inflict a lot of damage on Deathwing's high health pool. Secondly, nimble Assassins like Zeratul, Valla, or Tracer have an easy time dodging and thus diminishing a lot of Deathwing's damage due to long casting animations on most of his abilities.

maps.explanation:
Deathwing excels on Maps where the Objective gives vision and needs to be channeled (so Cursed Hollow and Garden of Terror) because he can use Skyfall at Level 7 to interrupt enemy Heroes without exposing himself.

While he is fine being in lane on his own, we do not recommend playing him on big Maps where teams tend to split a lot because Deathwing works best when accompanied by other Heroes who can setup for Molten Flame.

Contrary to other global Heroes, he does not provide much value on big Maps because the time it takes for Deathwing to use Dragonflight for going from a lane to another is too slow.

builds.name: Dragonflight Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Deathwing's Dragonflight Build is a powerful choice for games where you can safely land on top of enemy Heroes after your Tank engages or when the enemy team dives.

The combination of Dragon Soul at Level 1 and Heat Wave at Level 4 boosts your damage and survivability. Later in the game, Fire and Fury at Level 13 further empowers Deathwing's overall power when fighting at melee range.

The key Talents of this Build, however, are Death Drop at Level 7 indirectly increasing the damage dealt by allied Heroes and Gaze Onto Destruction at Level 16 reducing the damage dealt by enemy Heroes while also Slowing them.

When playing this Build, you should use Destroyer Form when you can play aggressively or World Breaker Form when you have to play defensively.

builds.name: Basic Attacks Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Deathwing's Basic Attacks Build makes you harder to kill and increases your damage at the same time, especially when you can fight at melee range.

The combination of Dragon Soul at Level 1 and Heat Wave at Level 4 boosts your damage and survivability. Later in the game, Fire and Fury at Level 13 further empowers Deathwing's overall power when fighting at melee range and Elementium Plating at Level 16 increases your survivability even more.

When playing this Build, you should use Destroyer Form when you can play aggressively or World Breaker Form when you have to play defensively.

builds.name: Molten Flame Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Deathwing's Molten Flame Build empowers the damage you can deal from the distance to enemy Heroes caught within Molten Flame for a few seconds.

The damage comes from the combination of multiple Talents that empower the same Basic Ability: Infernus at Level 4, Wicked Inferno at Level 13, and Conflagration at Level 16.

To get the most value out of this Build, you should only cast Molten Flame when having 75 Energy or higher. This means that, even if you are full Energy, you can only afford to cast one different Basic Ability before it: either Lava Burst or Earth Shatter.

When playing this Build, you should heavily prefer World Breaker Form.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Deathwing's ARAM Build is a powerful choice for games where you can safely land on top of enemy Heroes after your Tank engages or when the enemy team dives.

The combination of Dragon Soul at Level 1 and Heat Wave at Level 4 boosts your damage and survivability. Later in the game, Fire and Fury at Level 13 further empowers Deathwing's overall power when fighting at melee range.

The key Talents of this Build, however, are Death Drop at Level 7 indirectly increasing the damage dealt by allied Heroes and Gaze Onto Destruction at Level 16 reducing the damage dealt by enemy Heroes while also Slowing them.

When playing this Build, you should use Destroyer Form when you can play aggressively or World Breaker Form when you have to play defensively.

name: Deckard
overview: Deckard is a Healer specialized in single-target healing, with the possibility to prepare Healing Potion on the ground for later usage, and crowd control, usually used as follow-up to your Tank's engage.
strengths: Strong and efficient single-target healing output
Powerful area of effect crowd control
Access to Emerald for healing reduction
weaknesses: No access to Cleanse or similar tools to remove crowd-control effects

synergies.explanation:
Scroll Of Sealing makes Deckard excellent at following up on Heroes that can provide their own source of reliable crowd control (for example Johanna) and similarly good at setting up enemy Heroes for allied skillshot-based Abilities (such as Kel'Thuzad).

Healing Potion is extremely easy to use for healing allied Heroes without mobility, so they are great to have on Deckard's side. For the same reason, you should avoid picking high-mobility Heroes and/or dive Heroes.

counters.explanation:
With little in the way of mobility, Deckard struggles against Heroes who can easily engage on him, especially if they are ranged.

Heroes who have access to Unstoppable effects have easy life against Deckard as they can ignore all his offensive Abilities. Similarly, Cleanse effects (for example Intercession by Whitemane) are good against Deckard because they basically deny his main strength: crowd control.

Deckard can make up for his weakness to burst damage by taking short fights, however, the enemy team will usually still have an edge during them.

maps.explanation:
Deckard tends to do well on Maps that feature many choke points, where he is able to get value from Scroll Of Sealing and his Heroic Ability: Stay Awhile and Listen or Lorenado. Battlegrounds with a lot of wide areas (such as Hanamura Temple) will obviously make this characteristic harder to exploit.

The way Healing Potion works is particularly good when contesting powerful Objectives that take a long time to be secured (for example Shrines on Infernal Shrines). Having to move too much on the battlefield means you will get less value out of the potion-stocking aspect.

builds.name: Sapphire Emerald Build
builds.label: Recommended
builds.description:
Deckard's Sapphire Emerald Build increases your burst healing as well as your crowd control and utility. Due to its nature, this Build excels in short team fights.

Sapphire at Level 1 can be used to engage for your team and/or as a setup Scroll Of Sealing. Emerald at Level 7 should be used on the kill target, so that the Healer will not be able to save them.

Thanks to the Shield it provides, Potion of Shielding at Level 4 helps you keep alive whoever is being focused by enemy Heroes. Horadric Staff at Level 16 can be used to peel for allied Heroes and/or counter-engage.

builds.name: Ruby Emerald Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Deckard's Ruby Emerald Build increases your sustain healing and utility at the cost of crowd control. Due to its nature, this Build excels in long team fights.

Ruby at Level 4 is best used on multiple enemy Heroes when they are surrounding allied Heroes, to spawn more Lesser Healing Potions near your teammates. Emerald at Level 7 should be used on the kill target, so that the Healer will not be able to save them.

Field Study at Level 1 increases your Spell Power, which not only increases your damage done with Abilities but also your healing done. Safety in Numbers at Level 16 further increases the value you get from your Basic Abilities by reducing their cooldown.

builds.name: Sapphire Ruby Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Deckard's Sapphire Ruby Build provides a balanced mix of sustain and burst healing, crowd control, and utility. Due to its nature, this Build excels against 3 or more melee Heroes.

Sapphire at Level 1 can be used to engage for your team and/or as a setup Scroll Of Sealing. Ruby at Level 4 is best used on multiple enemy Heroes when they are surrounding allied Heroes, to spawn more Lesser Healing Potions near your teammates.

Kanai's Cube at Level 7 is a good defensive tool usable for reducing the effectiveness of dive Heroes. Scroll of Stone Curse at Level 16 can be used to deal damage to enemy Heroes who tend to group while figthing.

builds.name: Emerald Build
builds.label: Situational
builds.description:
Deckard's Emerald Build increases your sustain healing and healing reduction. Due to its nature, this Build excels against team compositions featuring multiple Healers.

Emerald at Level 7 should be used on the kill target, so that the Healer will not be able to save them. Once you get Perfect Gems at Level 20, you will be able to reduce enemy healing more often.

Super Healing Potion at Level 13 and Safety in Numbers at Level 16 combined together will greatly improve your sustain healing, which is great for the long team fights that happen when the enemy team has multiple Healers.

builds.name: ARAM Build
builds.label: ARAM
builds.description:
Deckard's ARAM Build increases your damage against enemy Heroes who tend to group. This damage scales as the game goes and spikes at Level 16. We find this Build particularly effective when there is another Healer in your team.

The synergy between Scroll of Identify at Level 1 and Scroll of Stone Curse at Level 16 allows you to deal a lot of damage to enemy Heroes who get caught inside Scroll Of Sealing. Cube Mastery at Level 7 lets you do that more often.
